images.note: Cliff Fragua's 2005 pink-Tennessee-marble Po'pay statue in the National Statuary Hall Collection (Emancipation Hall), U.S. Capitol; knotted cord visible in his left hand — the cord the runners carried to synchronize the revolt. Later artwork (2005), no contemporary likeness exists.
images.title: Po'pay statue by Cliff Fragua (2005), U.S. Capitol

images.note: Coronelli's Le Nouveau Mexique (first issued 1688/1689), drawn from Diego de Peñalosa's reports; shows the Rio Grande valley, pueblos, and Santa Fe on the eve of the revolt. Contemporary map (drawn 8 years after 1680).
images.title: Vincenzo Coronelli, Le Nouveau Mexique (1688), New Mexico

images.note: Edward S. Curtis, 'The Kiva Stairs—San Ildefonso' (1925): ladder descending into a kiva at San Ildefonso, a Tewa pueblo like Popé's Ohkay Owingeh. The underground ceremonial rooms the Franciscans invaded and banned. Later photograph; no qualifying alt from a different institution found (honest gap).
images.title: Kiva stairs at San Ildefonso Pueblo (Curtis, 1925)

images.note: Ca. 1910 photographic postcard of the San Francisco de Asís Mission Church, Ranchos de Taos — adobe mission architecture of the Franciscan mission system (encomienda labor, banned kivas, burned masks). Later photograph; no qualifying alt from a different institution found (honest gap).
images.title: San Francisco de Asís Mission Church, Ranchos de Taos (ca. 1910 postcard)
